```{r}
# source("load_data.R")
dataset <- redivis::user("datapages")$dataset("Numberbank")
hc <- dataset$table("highest count")$to_tibble()
kld <- dataset$table("knower level")$to_tibble()
```

```{r import manynumbers give-n}
# ManyNumbers Give-N import --------------------------------------------------
# Raw per-participant site exports arrive in pairs, named like:
#   {site}_{participant}_{qualtrics_id}_longformgiventaskV##.csv  (one row per trial)
#   {site}_{participant}_{qualtrics_id}_summary_giventaskV##.csv  (pre-computed per-query summary + KnowerLevel)
# Point mn_giventask_dir at the folder holding all such pairs (currently just
# the two example files in MN_code/) as more sites' data comes in. This folds
# ManyNumbers into td's schema below as dataset_id "ManyNumbers".
mn_giventask_dir <- "MN_simulated_data"

mn_longform_files <- Sys.glob(file.path(mn_giventask_dir, "*_longformgiventaskV*.csv"))
mn_summary_files  <- Sys.glob(file.path(mn_giventask_dir, "*_summary_giventaskV*.csv"))
mn_demographics_files <- Sys.glob(file.path(mn_giventask_dir, "ManyNumbers_forsharing_DataEntry_*.csv"))

# Read demographic file.
# Only age (from Dem_DOB/Dem_DOT), language, country, and gender are pulled
# in for now.
read_mn_demographics <- function(path) {
  raw <- read.csv(path, header = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE)
  raw <- raw[-c(1, 2), ] # drop the question-text + ImportId rows
  raw |>
    filter(trimws(ResponseId) != "") |>
    transmute(
      qualtrics_id = trimws(ResponseId),
      dob = suppressWarnings(as.Date(Dem_DOB, format = "%m/%d/%y")),
      dot = suppressWarnings(as.Date(Dem_DOT, format = "%m/%d/%y")),
      age = as.integer(round(as.numeric(difftime(dot, dob, units = "days")) / 30.4368)), # months
      gender = Dem_Gender,
      language = Dem_Language,
      country = Q10,
      export_mtime = file.info(path)$mtime
    )
}

# multiple exports may exist over time (new Qualtrics downloads); keep the
# most recently exported row per response
mn_demographics <- if (length(mn_demographics_files)) {
  bind_rows(lapply(mn_demographics_files, read_mn_demographics)) |>
    arrange(qualtrics_id, desc(export_mtime)) |>
    distinct(qualtrics_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
    select(-export_mtime)
} else {
  tibble(qualtrics_id = character(), age = integer(), gender = character(),
         language = character(), country = character())
}

read_mn_longform <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    mutate(query = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gn_Query)),
           response = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gn_Response))) |>
    filter(!is.na(query), !is.na(response)) |>
    transmute(
      dataset_id = "ManyNumbers",
      subject_id = paste(gn_siteid, gn_participant, sep = "_"), 
      qualtrics_id = trimws(gn_qualtrics_id),
      method = "non-titrated", # fixed give-n protocol
      query = query,
      response = pmin(response, 10) # cap at 10, matching trial_data convention
    )
}

# Reshape KL labels into numberbank convention
label_to_kl <- function(label, cp_threshold = 6) {
  kl_numeric <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(gsub("-knower", "", label, ignore.case = TRUE)))
  kl_numeric[tolower(label) == "pre-knower"] <- 0
  if_else(is.na(kl_numeric), NA_character_,
          if_else(kl_numeric >= cp_threshold, "CP-knower", paste0(kl_numeric, "-knower")))
}

label_to_kl_subset <- function(label, cp_threshold = 6) {
  kl <- label_to_kl(label, cp_threshold)
  case_when(
    is.na(kl) ~ NA_character_,
    kl == "CP-knower" ~ "CP-knower",
    kl == "0-knower" ~ "Pre-knower",
    .default = "Subset-knower"
  )
}

read_mn_summary <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    transmute(subject_id = participant, KnowerLevel)
}

mn_longform_raw <- if (length(mn_longform_files)) bind_rows(lapply(mn_longform_files, read_mn_longform)) else
  tibble(dataset_id = character(), subject_id = character(), qualtrics_id = character(),
         method = character(), query = integer(), response = integer())

# Highest Count task, named like {site}_{participant}_{qualtrics_id}_highestcounttask.csv
mn_hc_files <- Sys.glob(file.path(mn_giventask_dir, "*_highestcounttask.csv"))

read_mn_hc <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    transmute(
      subject_id = paste(hc_siteid, hc_participant, sep = "_"),
      qualtrics_id = trimws(hc_qualtrics_id),
      hc = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(hc_highestcount))
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(hc))
}

mn_hc <- if (length(mn_hc_files)) bind_rows(lapply(mn_hc_files, read_mn_hc)) else
  tibble(subject_id = character(), qualtrics_id = character(), hc = numeric())

# combines both sources so a participant who only did the Highest Count task
# (no Give-N submission) still resolves a qualtrics_id for the demographics
# lookup below
mn_subject_qualtrics <- bind_rows(
  mn_longform_raw |> distinct(subject_id, qualtrics_id),
  mn_hc |> distinct(subject_id, qualtrics_id)
) |> distinct(subject_id, qualtrics_id)

# one KnowerLevel per participant (the summary file repeats it once per
# query row, so take the first)
mn_summary_kl <- if (length(mn_summary_files)) {
  bind_rows(lapply(mn_summary_files, read_mn_summary)) |>
    group_by(subject_id) |>
    summarise(KnowerLevel = first(KnowerLevel), .groups = "drop")
} else {
  tibble(subject_id = character(), KnowerLevel = character())
}

# kld-shaped table for ManyNumbers: every subject who has either a Give-N
# summary or a Highest Count submission (or both), same as how Numberbank's
# own kld can have kl-only, hc-only, or both -- with age/language/country
# merged in from demographics via qualtrics_id
mn_kld <- full_join(mn_summary_kl, mn_hc |> select(subject_id, hc), by = "subject_id") |>
  left_join(mn_subject_qualtrics, by = "subject_id") |>
  left_join(mn_demographics |> select(qualtrics_id, age, language, country), by = "qualtrics_id") |>
  transmute(
    dataset_id = "ManyNumbers",
    subject_id,
    age,
    language,
    country,
    method = "non-titrated",
    kl = label_to_kl(KnowerLevel),
    kl_subset = label_to_kl_subset(KnowerLevel),
    hc
  )

# trial-level ManyNumbers rows also need kl/kl_subset attached (from mn_kld
# above) -- td's own kl/kl_subset columns are what the Plots -- Items tab
# filters trials by, so without this every ManyNumbers trial silently fails
# that filter and never renders there, no matter how much data exists
mn_td <- mn_longform_raw |>
  left_join(mn_demographics |> select(qualtrics_id, age, language, country), by = "qualtrics_id") |>
  left_join(mn_kld |> select(subject_id, kl, kl_subset), by = "subject_id") |>
  select(dataset_id, subject_id, method, age, language, country, query, response, kl, kl_subset)

# combined trial-level data: Numberbank's own td plus the newly imported
# ManyNumbers trials, in the same shape
td_all <- bind_rows(td, mn_td)

# datasets not yet in kld at all: currently just ManyNumbers, whose kl comes
# from mn_kld above (built from the site's own summary file) rather than the
# recalculation below. 
# td also has several older studies with no kld rows yet
# (e.g. Krajcsi2018, Sarnecka2007, the Boni/Marchand/Wagner sets), we might 
# need to address that
new_datasets <- c("ManyNumbers")
```

```{r recalculate kl}
source("data/kl_calc_mn.R")
source("data/helpers/mn_gn_knowerlevel_details.R")

# recalculate_kl_mn(_details) match trials into sessions by exact age, and
# NA != NA, so give ManyNumbers rows a fake age for this call only
# where their real (demographics-derived) age is still missing. Note
# ManyNumbers' kl in kl_final comes from mn_kld (the summary file), not from
# this recalculation -- this is only run so we have a from-raw-trials
# cross-check (mn_kl_qc below) and so existing kld-tracked datasets keep
# working exactly as before.
td_for_recalc <- td_all |> mutate(age = if_else(dataset_id %in% new_datasets & is.na(age), -1L, age))
kl_recalc <- recalculate_kl_mn(td_for_recalc, hc)
kl_recalc_details <- recalculate_kl_mn_details(td_for_recalc)

# QC check: does recomputing kl from raw trial responses agree with the
# KnowerLevel the site's own summary file already gives us (the value we
# actually use, via mn_kld)?
mn_kl_qc <- kl_recalc |>
  filter(dataset_id == "ManyNumbers") |>
  select(-age) |>
  left_join(mn_kld |> select(subject_id, kl_from_summary = kl), by = "subject_id") |>
  mutate(kl_match = kl == kl_from_summary)
```

```{r}
# replacement language values
language_recode <- list(
  "Arabic" = "Saudi",
  "French" = "Français",
  "English" = c("Anglais", "English (India)", "English (US)", "English/Portugese", "English/Spanish"),
  "Slovenian (dual)" = "Slovenian_dual",
  "Slovenian (non-dual)" = c("Slovenian", "Slovenian_nonDual", "Serbian/Slovenian")
)

languages_countries <- bind_rows(kld |> select(language, country), td_all |> select(language, country)) |>
  distinct() |>
  mutate(# recode + sort languages
         lang = language |> fct_collapse(!!!language_recode) |> fct_relevel(sort),
         # combination of language and country
         language_country = paste(lang, country, sep = "\n")) |>
  distinct(language, lang, country, language_country) |>
  group_by(lang) |>
  mutate(language_countries = paste(unique(country), collapse = ", "),
         language_countries = glue("{lang} – {language_countries}")) |>
  group_by(country) |>
  mutate(country_languages = paste(unique(lang), collapse = ", "),
         country_languages = glue("{country} – {country_languages}")) |>
  ungroup()

# a study/method is eligible for the recalculated knower level only if it
# uses a non-titrated method and tests all of the numbers 1 through 6
kl_source_eligibility <- td_all |>
  group_by(dataset_id, method) |>
  summarise(tests_1_to_6 = all(1:6 %in% query), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(use_recalc = method == "non-titrated" & tests_1_to_6) |>
  select(dataset_id, method, use_recalc)

# some older studies were uploaded to the "trials" table (td) but were never
# given an official row in the "knower level" table (kld) at all -- so they
# don't show up anywhere in the knower-level plots, even though we have their
# raw trial data. Add them to kld here using the same recalculation already
# computed above (kl_recalc), restricted to the same eligibility rule used
# everywhere else (kl_source_eligibility): non-titrated, and testing all of
# 1 through 6.
# This added 4 datasets to the list.
kld_gap_datasets <- setdiff(unique(td$dataset_id), unique(kld$dataset_id))

kld_gap_rows <- kl_recalc |>
  filter(dataset_id %in% kld_gap_datasets) |>
  semi_join(kl_source_eligibility |> filter(use_recalc), by = c("dataset_id", "method")) |>
  select(dataset_id, subject_id, age, language, country, method, kl, kl_subset, hc)

kld <- bind_rows(kld, kld_gap_rows)

# td's own kl/kl_subset should also reflect the recalculated classification
# when eligible, so Plots -- Items (which reads straight from
# trial_data/td_all) stays consistent with Plots -- Knower levels (which
# reads kl_data/kl_final) for the same trials. ManyNumbers is excluded here
# since it already got its authoritative kl merged in from its own summary
# files above (see mn_td) -- recomputing it from trial responses would
# override that on-purpose choice.
td_all <- td_all |>
  left_join(kl_source_eligibility, by = c("dataset_id", "method")) |>
  mutate(use_recalc = coalesce(use_recalc, FALSE) & !(dataset_id %in% new_datasets)) |>
  left_join(
    kl_recalc |> select(dataset_id, subject_id, age, method, kl_recalc = kl, kl_subset_recalc = kl_subset),
    by = c("dataset_id", "subject_id", "age", "method")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    kl = if_else(use_recalc & !is.na(kl_recalc), kl_recalc, kl),
    kl_subset = if_else(use_recalc & !is.na(kl_recalc), kl_subset_recalc, kl_subset)
  ) |>
  select(-use_recalc, -kl_recalc, -kl_subset_recalc)

# kld left untouched; kl_final swaps in the recalculated kl/kl_subset only for
# eligible study/methods, falling back to kld's values everywhere else
# NOTE: this only affects Piantadosi & Gibson's data, because they only ask each kid for 1 trial per number.
kl_final <- bind_rows(
  kld |>
    left_join(kl_source_eligibility, by = c("dataset_id", "method")) |>
    mutate(use_recalc = coalesce(use_recalc, FALSE)) |>
    left_join(
      kl_recalc |> select(dataset_id, subject_id, age, method, kl_recalc = kl, kl_subset_recalc = kl_subset),
      by = c("dataset_id", "subject_id", "age", "method")
    ) |>
    mutate(
      kl = if_else(use_recalc & !is.na(kl_recalc), kl_recalc, kl),
      kl_subset = if_else(use_recalc & !is.na(kl_recalc), kl_subset_recalc, kl_subset)
    ) |>
    select(-use_recalc, -kl_recalc, -kl_subset_recalc),
  # MN gets KL from own summary files, 
  mn_kld
)

kl_data <- kl_final |>
  filter(!is.na(kl) | !is.na(hc)) |> # remove rows with both kl and hc NA
  left_join(languages_countries) |> mutate(language = lang) |> select(-lang) |>
  arrange(language, kl, age)

trial_data <- td_all |>
  mutate(response = if_else(response > 10, 10, response)) |> # cap responses at 10
  left_join(languages_countries) |> mutate(language = lang) |> select(-lang)
  # mutate(# recode + sort languages
  #        language = language |> fct_collapse(!!!language_recode) |> fct_relevel(sort),
  #        # combination of language and country
  #        language_country = paste(language, country, sep = "\n"))
```

```{r import manynumbers ams+vm}
# ManyNumbers Dot Comparison (AMS) + Visual Memory (VM) import --------------
# Raw per-participant site exports are named like:
#   {site}_{participant}_{id}_amstaskorganizedfile.csv  (one row per AMS trial)
#   {site}_{participant}_{id}_vmtaskorganizedfile.csv   (one row per VM trial)
# Unlike the Give-N/demographics files, these carry their own age/language
# columns directly (age_years/age_months/Language) and have no qualtrics id
# of their own -- see manynumbers_datadictionary_030326_V01.pdf. Country
# isn't part of either file, so it's backfilled from the Give-N demographics
# import above where the same subject_id also has a Give-N submission; a
# subject with AMS/VM data but no Give-N/demographics (e.g. a lone AMS-only
# submission) will end up with country = NA and so won't match any
# country/language sidebar filter.
mn_ams_files <- Sys.glob(file.path(mn_giventask_dir, "*_amstaskorganizedfile.csv"))
mn_vm_files  <- Sys.glob(file.path(mn_giventask_dir, "*_vmtaskorganizedfile.csv"))

read_mn_ams <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    filter(block %in% c("block1", "block2", "block3")) |> # experimental trials only, drop sample/practice
    transmute(
      dataset_id = "ManyNumbers",
      subject_id = paste(SiteID, participant, sep = "_"),
      age = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(age_months)),
      language = Language,
      numRatio = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(numRatio)),
      accuracy = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(accuracy)),
      rt = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(rt))
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(accuracy))
}

read_mn_vm <- function(path) {
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
    transmute(
      dataset_id = "ManyNumbers",
      subject_id = paste(SiteID, participant, sep = "_"),
      age = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(age_months)),
      language = Language,
      clicks = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(clicks)),
      accuracy = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(accuracy)),
      rt = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(rt))
    ) |>
    filter(!is.na(accuracy))
}

mn_ams_raw <- if (length(mn_ams_files)) bind_rows(lapply(mn_ams_files, read_mn_ams)) else
  tibble(dataset_id = character(), subject_id = character(), age = numeric(),
         language = character(), numRatio = numeric(), accuracy = numeric(), rt = numeric())

mn_vm_raw <- if (length(mn_vm_files)) bind_rows(lapply(mn_vm_files, read_mn_vm)) else
  tibble(dataset_id = character(), subject_id = character(), age = numeric(),
         language = character(), clicks = numeric(), accuracy = numeric(), rt = numeric())

# country + knower level backfilled by subject_id from the Give-N import
# above (mn_subject_qualtrics/mn_demographics/mn_kld); a subject with no
# Give-N submission gets NA for both, same caveat as above for country
mn_subject_country <- mn_subject_qualtrics |>
  left_join(mn_demographics |> select(qualtrics_id, country), by = "qualtrics_id") |>
  distinct(subject_id, country)

mn_subject_kl <- mn_kld |> distinct(subject_id, kl, kl_subset)

# split the (language, country) lookup in two so a subject with no country
# (no matching Give-N submission to backfill it from) still resolves a
# recoded language/language_countries -- language_countries is aggregated
# per language across all its countries, so it doesn't actually need country
# to be known. Only language_country/country_languages genuinely require it
# and stay NA without one.
lang_lookup <- languages_countries |> distinct(language, lang, language_countries)
country_lookup <- languages_countries |> distinct(language, country, language_country, country_languages)

attach_mn_lookups <- function(df) {
  df |>
    left_join(mn_subject_country, by = "subject_id") |>
    left_join(mn_subject_kl, by = "subject_id") |>
    left_join(lang_lookup, by = "language") |>
    left_join(country_lookup, by = c("language", "country")) |>
    mutate(language = lang) |>
    select(-lang)
}

ams_data <- mn_ams_raw |> attach_mn_lookups()
vm_data <- mn_vm_raw |> attach_mn_lookups()
```

```{r}
td_subjects <- td |> distinct(dataset_id, subject_id)
kld_subjects <- kld |> distinct(dataset_id, subject_id)

# in td but not in kld
only_in_td <- td_subjects |> anti_join(kld_subjects, by = c("dataset_id", "subject_id"))

# in kld but not in td
only_in_kld <- kld_subjects |> anti_join(td_subjects, by = c("dataset_id", "subject_id"))

# combined, labeled with which dataset each came from
diff_subjects <- bind_rows(
  only_in_td |> mutate(in_dataset = "td_only"),
  only_in_kld |> mutate(in_dataset = "kld_only")
)
```

```{r compare with existing kld}
# subjects present in both
comparison <- kld |>
  select(dataset_id, subject_id, age, method, kl_kld = kl, kl_subset_kld = kl_subset) |>
  inner_join(
    kl_recalc |> select(dataset_id, subject_id, age, method, kl_recalc = kl, kl_subset_recalc = kl_subset),
    by = c("dataset_id", "subject_id", "age", "method")
  )

# subjects missing from one side or the other
only_in_kld <- kld |> anti_join(kl_recalc, by = c("dataset_id", "subject_id", "age", "method"))
only_in_recalc <- kl_recalc |> anti_join(kld, by = c("dataset_id", "subject_id", "age", "method"))

# the actual disagreements, for closer inspection
mismatches <- comparison |> filter(kl_kld != kl_recalc)
```

```{r}
library(tidyr)
# long format: one row per study x method x number, with trial count
study_query_summary <- td_all |>
  count(dataset_id, method, query, name = "n_trials") |>
  arrange(dataset_id, method, query)

# wide format: one row per study x method, one column per number asked
study_query_wide <- study_query_summary |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = query, values_from = n_trials, values_fill = 0, names_prefix = "query_")

# compact summary: just the set of numbers each study/method asked for
study_query_range <- td_all |>
  group_by(dataset_id, method) |>
  summarise(numbers_asked = paste(sort(unique(query)), collapse = ", "), .groups = "drop")
```

```{r dataset browser summary}
# one row per dataset, computed from what's already loaded above (kl_data +
# td_all) -- feeds the preview panel built into the "Datasets" filter below.
# Built from kl_data (not kl_final) so this always matches exactly the set of
# datasets the filter itself offers.
dataset_kl_summary <- kl_data |>
  group_by(dataset_id) |>
  summarise(
    n_subjects = n(),
    age_min = { v <- suppressWarnings(min(age, na.rm = TRUE)); if (is.infinite(v)) NA_integer_ else v },
    age_max = { v <- suppressWarnings(max(age, na.rm = TRUE)); if (is.infinite(v)) NA_integer_ else v },
    methods = paste(sort(unique(method)), collapse = ", "),
    languages = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(language))), collapse = ", "),
    countries = paste(sort(unique(na.omit(country))), collapse = ", "),
    n_pre = sum(kl_subset == "Pre-knower", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_subset = sum(kl_subset == "Subset-knower", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_cp = sum(kl_subset == "CP-knower", na.rm = TRUE),
    n_classified = sum(!is.na(kl)),
    n_with_hc = sum(!is.na(hc)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

dataset_trial_summary <- td_all |>
  group_by(dataset_id) |>
  summarise(
    has_trial_data = TRUE,
    n_trials = n(),
    numbers_tested = paste(sort(unique(query)), collapse = ", "),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# use these functions to populate the dataset filter with badges denoting 
# which dataset includes which task.
dataset_ams_summary <- ams_data |>
  group_by(dataset_id) |>
  summarise(n_with_ams = n_distinct(subject_id), .groups = "drop")

dataset_vm_summary <- vm_data |>
  group_by(dataset_id) |>
  summarise(n_with_vm = n_distinct(subject_id), .groups = "drop")

# curated description/citation/link, filled in by hand from
# data/study_metadata_template.csv -- most rows are still blank (only
# ManyNumbers has real content so far), which the preview panel below shows
# as the usual "no description on file yet" empty state
study_metadata <- read.csv("study_metadata_template.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, na.strings = "") |>
  rename(title_override = title)

dataset_browser_data <- dataset_kl_summary |>
  left_join(dataset_trial_summary, by = "dataset_id") |>
  mutate(has_trial_data = coalesce(has_trial_data, FALSE)) |>
  left_join(dataset_ams_summary, by = "dataset_id") |>
  left_join(dataset_vm_summary, by = "dataset_id") |>
  mutate(n_with_ams = coalesce(n_with_ams, 0L), n_with_vm = coalesce(n_with_vm, 0L)) |>
  left_join(study_metadata, by = "dataset_id") |>
  arrange(title_override)
```

```{r}
ojs_define(hc = hc)
ojs_define(kl_data = kl_data)
ojs_define(trial_data = trial_data)
ojs_define(dataset_browser_data = dataset_browser_data)
ojs_define(ams_data = ams_data)
ojs_define(vm_data = vm_data)
```

```{ojs}
// dataset preview panel, built into the "Datasets" filter below -----------
dp_raw = transpose(dataset_browser_data)

dp_pct = (part, whole) => whole > 0 ? Math.round((part / whole) * 100) : 0

dp_datasets = dp_raw.map(r => {
  const c = r.n_classified || 1;
  return {
    id: r.dataset_id,
    title: r.title_override || r.dataset_id.replace(/_/g, " "),
    description: r.short_description,
    citation: r.citation,
    link: r.link,
    n: r.n_subjects,
    ageMin: r.age_min, ageMax: r.age_max,
    languages: r.languages ? r.languages.split(", ") : [],
    countries: r.countries ? r.countries.split(", ") : [],
    methods: r.methods ? r.methods.split(", ").map(m => "Give-N · " + m) : [],
    numbersTested: r.numbers_tested,
    hasTrialData: r.has_trial_data,
    nTrials: r.n_trials,
    nWithHc: r.n_with_hc,
    nWithAms: r.n_with_ams, 
    nWithVm: r.n_with_vm, 
    isLiveImport: r.dataset_id === "ManyNumbers",
    kl: { pre: dp_pct(r.n_pre, c), subset: dp_pct(r.n_subset, c), cp: dp_pct(r.n_cp, c) },
  };
})
```

```{ojs}
dp_klColor = ({ pre: "#2a78d6", subset: "#eb6834", cp: "#1baf7a" })

function dp_klBar(d, height) {
  return html`<div class="dp-kl-bar" style=${{height: height + "px"}}>
    <span title=${"Pre-knower " + d.kl.pre + "%"} style=${{width: d.kl.pre + "%", background: dp_klColor.pre}}></span>
    <span title=${"Subset-knower " + d.kl.subset + "%"} style=${{width: d.kl.subset + "%", background: dp_klColor.subset}}></span>
    <span title=${"CP-knower " + d.kl.cp + "%"} style=${{width: d.kl.cp + "%", background: dp_klColor.cp}}></span>
  </div>`;
}

function dp_expandContent(d) {
  const hasCuratedInfo = !!(d.description || d.citation || d.link);

  const curatedBlock = hasCuratedInfo
    ? html`<div class="dp-desc">
        ${d.description ? html`<p class="dp-fact">${d.description}</p>` : ""}
        ${d.citation ? html`<p class="dp-fact dp-citation">${d.citation}</p>` : ""}
        ${d.link ? html`<p class="dp-fact"><a href=${d.link} target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">${d.link}</a></p>` : ""}
      </div>`
    : html`<div class="dp-note">No study description, citation, or link on file yet.</div>`;

  const liveNote = d.isLiveImport
    ? html`<div class="dp-note live"><strong>Live import.</strong> Grows automatically as new
        ManyNumbers site submissions arrive — currently ${d.n} participants across ${d.countries.length} sites.</div>`
    : "";

  const trialFact = d.hasTrialData
    ? html`<p class="dp-fact"><b>${d.nTrials?.toLocaleString()}</b> trials logged${d.numbersTested ? html` · numbers tested <b>${d.numbersTested}</b>` : ""}</p>`
    : html`<p class="dp-fact">no trial-by-trial data on file</p>`;

  return html`<div class="dp-expand">
    <div class="dp-badge-row">${[
    ...d.methods,
    ...(d.nWithAms > 0 ? ["Dot Comparison"] : []),
    ...(d.nWithVm > 0 ? ["Visual Memory"] : []),
  ].map(m => html`<span class="dp-badge">${m}</span>`)}</div>
    ${curatedBlock}
    ${liveNote}
    <p class="dp-fact"><b>${d.n}</b> participants${d.ageMin != null ? html` · ages <b>${d.ageMin}–${d.ageMax} mo</b>` : ""}</p>
    <p class="dp-fact">Languages: ${d.languages.length ? d.languages.join(", ") : "—"}</p>
    <p class="dp-fact">Countries: ${d.countries.length ? d.countries.join(", ") : "—"}</p>
    ${trialFact}
    ${d.nWithHc > 0 ? html`<p class="dp-fact">Highest Count on file for <b>${d.nWithHc}</b> of ${d.n} participants</p>` : ""}
  </div>`;
}

// wraps any Inputs.select(..., {multiple: true}) view with "All"/"None"
// buttons that set its value and fire the same input event Observable's
// reactivity expects, so viewof cells built from this stay wired up exactly
// like the Inputs.select they wrap
function withAllNoneButtons(view, allValues) {
  const allBtn = html`<button type="button" class="filter-allnone-btn">All</button>`;
  const noneBtn = html`<button type="button" class="filter-allnone-btn">None</button>`;

  allBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    view.value = allValues.slice();
    view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
  });
  noneBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    view.value = [];
    view.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
  });

  const btnRow = html`<div class="filter-allnone-row">${allBtn}${noneBtn}</div>`;
  const wrap = html`<div>${view}${btnRow}</div>`;
  wrap.value = view.value;
  view.addEventListener("input", () => {
    wrap.value = view.value;
    wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input"));
  });
  return wrap;
}

// custom Observable view: either the checkbox or the study's title toggles
// whether that dataset_id is included in the real filters below
// (klf/trf/hcf), exactly like the Inputs.select this replaces. A separate
// "Study details" button expands an inline preview, accordion-style,
// without changing what's included.
function datasetPicker(datasets, defaultIds) {
  const root = html`<div class="dp-wrap"></div>`;
  const included = new Set(defaultIds);
  let expandedId = null;

  const search = html`<input class="dp-search" type="text" placeholder="Filter datasets…">`;
  const countLabel = html`<span class="dp-count"></span>`;
  const list = html`<ul class="dp-list"></ul>`;

  function notify() {
    root.value = Array.from(included);
    root.dispatchEvent(new Event("input", { bubbles: true }));
  }

  // "All"/"None" always apply to the full dataset list, not just whatever
  // the search box currently narrows the visible rows down to
  const allBtn = html`<button type="button" class="filter-allnone-btn">All</button>`;
  const noneBtn = html`<button type="button" class="filter-allnone-btn">None</button>`;
  allBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    for (const d of datasets) included.add(d.id);
    render();
    notify();
  });
  noneBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
    included.clear();
    render();
    notify();
  });
  const btnRow = html`<div class="filter-allnone-row">${allBtn}${noneBtn}</div>`;

  function render() {
    const q = search.value.trim().toLowerCase();
    const filtered = datasets.filter(d => {
      if (!q) return true;
      const hay = [d.title, d.id, ...d.languages, ...d.countries].join(" ").toLowerCase();
      return hay.includes(q);
    });

    countLabel.textContent = `${included.size} of ${datasets.length} included`;
    list.replaceChildren();

    for (const d of filtered) {
      const li = html`<li class="dp-item"></li>`;

      const cb = html`<input type="checkbox">`;
      cb.checked = included.has(d.id);
      cb.ariaLabel = `Include ${d.title}`;

      function setIncluded(isIncluded) {
        cb.checked = isIncluded;
        if (isIncluded) included.add(d.id); else included.delete(d.id);
        countLabel.textContent = `${included.size} of ${datasets.length} included`;
        notify();
      }

      cb.addEventListener("change", () => setIncluded(cb.checked));

      const titleBtn = html`<button type="button" class="dp-row-title-btn">
        <span class="dp-row-title">${d.title}</span>
        <span class="dp-row-sub">${d.id} · n=${d.n}</span>
      </button>`;
      titleBtn.addEventListener("click", () => setIncluded(!cb.checked));

      const microBar = dp_klBar(d, 6);
      microBar.className = "dp-microbar dp-kl-bar";

      const detailsBtn = html`<button type="button" class="dp-details-btn">${expandedId === d.id ? "Hide" : "Details"}</button>`;
      detailsBtn.setAttribute("aria-expanded", expandedId === d.id);
      detailsBtn.addEventListener("click", () => {
        expandedId = expandedId === d.id ? null : d.id;
        render();
      });

      const row = html`<div class="dp-row"></div>`;
      row.append(cb, titleBtn, microBar, detailsBtn);

      li.append(row);
      if (expandedId === d.id) li.append(dp_expandContent(d));

      list.append(li);
    }
  }

  search.addEventListener("input", render);
  root.append(search, btnRow, countLabel, list);
  render();

  root.value = Array.from(included);
  return root;
}
```

__Filter by...__
```{ojs}
// age filter
viewof ages = interval([d3.min(kl_data.age), d3.max(kl_data.age)],
                       {step: 1, label: "Age (months)"})

// kl filter
// explicit developmental order, covering both kl's values (0-5-knower,
// Subset-knower -- kld does have some rows only classified at that generic
// level, not a specific number -- and CP-knower) and kl_subset's values
// (Pre-knower, Subset-knower, CP-knower); falls back to alphabetical for
// anything unexpected so a new/unseen label doesn't silently disappear
kl_rank_order = ["Pre-knower", "0-knower", "1-knower", "2-knower", "3-knower",
                  "4-knower", "5-knower", "Subset-knower", "CP-knower"]
// some rows have kl = null (e.g. a subject with Highest Count data but no
// classifiable Give-N submission) -- those still need to sort somewhere
// without crashing on localeCompare(null); null always sorts last.
cp_sort = (a, b) => {
  if (a == null && b == null) return 0;
  if (a == null) return 1;
  if (b == null) return -1;
  const ia = kl_rank_order.indexOf(a), ib = kl_rank_order.indexOf(b);
  if (ia === -1 || ib === -1) return a.localeCompare(b);
  return ia - ib;
}
kl_vals = Array.from(new Set(kl_data.kl)).filter(v => v != null).sort(cp_sort) // options -- null excluded, it's not a selectable knower level
kl_defs = kl_vals.filter(s => /^[123C]/.test(s)) // default
viewof kls = withAllNoneButtons(Inputs.select(kl_vals, {label: "Knower levels", multiple: true, value: kl_defs}), kl_vals)

// kl subset toggle
viewof kl_sub = Inputs.checkbox(["Group non-CP-knowers together"])
kl_y = kl_sub.length ? "kl_subset" : "kl"

// method filter (titrated vs. non-titrated)
method_vals = Array.from(new Set(kl_data.method)).sort() // options
viewof methods = Inputs.checkbox(method_vals, {label: "Method", value: method_vals})

// language filter
lang_vals = Array.from(new Set(kl_data.language_countries)).sort() // options
lang_defs = lang_vals.filter(s => /English/.test(s))
viewof langs = withAllNoneButtons(Inputs.select(lang_vals, {label: "Languages", multiple: true, value: lang_defs}), lang_vals)

// country filter f
country_vals = Array.from(new Set(kl_data.country_languages)).sort() // options
country_defs = country_vals.filter(s => /English/.test(s))
viewof countries = withAllNoneButtons(Inputs.select(country_vals, {label: "Countries", multiple: true, value: country_defs}), country_vals)

// dataset filter -- checkbox list with an inline per-study preview
// (dp_datasets/datasetPicker are defined above, before the sidebar)
dataset_vals = Array.from(new Set(kl_data.dataset_id)).sort() // options
dataset_defs = dataset_vals // default
viewof datasets = {
  const label = html`Datasets`;
  const picker = datasetPicker(dp_datasets, dataset_defs);
  const wrap = html`<div>${label}${picker}</div>`;
  wrap.value = picker.value;
  picker.addEventListener("input", () => {
    wrap.value = picker.value;
    wrap.dispatchEvent(new Event("input"));
  });
  return wrap;
}
```

```{ojs}
// filter data using inputs (except age). This tab is specifically about
// knower level, so a row with no classifiable kl (e.g. Highest-Count-only
// submissions) never matches any kls selection -- it has no knower level to
// show here. (Highest Count below re-derives its own filtered set from `kl`
// so those rows aren't lost there.)
klf = kl.filter(d => langs.includes(d.language_countries))
        .filter(d => countries.includes(d.country_languages))
        .filter(d => datasets.includes(d.dataset_id))
        .filter(d => kls.includes(d.kl))
        .filter(d => methods.includes(d.method))
        .filter(d => d.age >= ages[0] && d.age <= ages[1])

// possible kl values in filtered data
klfv = Array.from(new Set(klf.map(d => d[kl_y]))).filter(v => v != null).sort(cp_sort)

kl_found = klf.length > 0
```

```{ojs}
// export: current view's data as CSV, plus an R snippet that reproduces the
// same filtered subset from the live pipeline -----------------------------
function downloadText(filename, text, mime = "text/plain") {
  const blob = new Blob([text], { type: mime });
  const url = URL.createObjectURL(blob);
  const a = document.createElement("a");
  a.href = url;
  a.download = filename;
  document.body.append(a);
  a.click();
  a.remove();
  URL.revokeObjectURL(url);
}

// R character-vector literal from an array of strings
function rVec(values) {
  const esc = s => `"${String(s).replace(/\\/g, "\\\\").replace(/"/g, '\\"')}"`;
  if (values.length === 0) return "character(0)";
  return `c(${values.map(esc).join(", ")})`;
}

// the R equivalent of the sidebar filters currently applied to klf/trf,
// exactly as they're applied in JS above -- extraLines lets a view (e.g.
// Highest Count) add its own additional condition (e.g. !is.na(hc))
function buildFilterRCode(baseVar, extraLines = []) {
  const lines = [
    `filter(language_countries %in% ${rVec(langs)})`,
    `filter(country_languages %in% ${rVec(countries)})`,
    `filter(dataset_id %in% ${rVec(datasets)})`,
    `filter(kl %in% ${rVec(kls)})`,
    `filter(method %in% ${rVec(methods)})`,
    `filter(age >= ${ages[0]}, age <= ${ages[1]})`,
    ...extraLines,
  ];
  return `${baseVar} |>\n  ${lines.join(" |>\n  ")}`;
}

// viewLabel: short slug for filenames. baseVar: "kl_data" or "trial_data" --
// the R object the snippet re-filters. rows: the already-filtered JS array
// (klf/trf/hcf) to write out as CSV. extraLines: additional R filter() calls
// beyond the standard sidebar filters (e.g. Highest Count's !is.na(hc)).
function exportView(viewLabel, baseVar, rows, extraLines = []) {
  downloadText(`numberbank_${viewLabel}.csv`, d3.csvFormat(rows), "text/csv");

  const rCode = `# Numberbank -- ${viewLabel}
# Generated ${new Date().toISOString()} from the filters selected on this page.
#
# This reproduces the *live* filtered subset from the pipeline (needs the
# numberbank-2026 repo and Redivis access -- see data/load_numberbank.R).
# For a fixed snapshot of exactly what you saw, use the CSV downloaded
# alongside this file instead -- the live data may have grown since then.

source("data/load_numberbank.R")
library(dplyr)

${viewLabel}_data <- ${buildFilterRCode(baseVar, extraLines)}
`;
  downloadText(`numberbank_${viewLabel}.R`, rCode);
}
```

```{ojs}
  return html`<div class="export-row">${btn}<p class="export-note">Downloads a CSV of the ${trf.length} trials shown below, plus an R script that reproduces this filtered selection.</p></div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
html`${tr_found ? '' : filter_error}`
```

```{ojs}
rc_map = d3.rollup(trf, v => v.length, d => d[kl_y], d => d.query, d => d.response)

rc = Array.from(rc_map, ([kl, kl_responses]) =>
  Array.from(kl_responses, ([query, query_responses]) => 
    Array.from(query_responses, ([response, count]) =>
      ({ kl, query, response, count, total: d3.sum(query_responses.values())})
    ).map(d => ({ ...d, proportion: d.count / d.total }))
  ).flat()
).flat()

tr_found ? Plot.plot({
  title: "Distribution of responses by knower level",
  style: { fontFamily: fontFamily, fontSize: fontSize },
  width: 950,
  height: 120 * rc_map.size,
  marginRight: 100,
  x: { label: "Response" },
  y: { label: "Proportion responses", grid: true, domain: [0, 1] },
  fx: { label: "Query" },
  fy: { label: null, padding: 0.2, domain: klfv },
  color: { domain: klfv },
  marks: [
    Plot.rectY(rc, {
      x: "response",
      y: "proportion",
      fx: "query",
      fy: "kl",
      fill: "kl",
      padding: 0.03
    }),
    Plot.axisX({ facetAnchor: null }),
    Plot.axisY({ facetAnchor: "left", labelAnchor: "center", labelArrow: "none" }),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
}) : html``
```

## Highest Count

{{< include md/disclaimer-hc.md >}}

```{ojs}
// built from `kl` (not klf) since Highest Count isn't gated on having a
// classifiable knower level -- a null kl always passes here, matching the
// same-shaped filters on amsf/vmf below.
hcf = kl.filter(d => langs.includes(d.language_countries))
        .filter(d => countries.includes(d.country_languages))
        .filter(d => datasets.includes(d.dataset_id))
        .filter(d => kls.includes(d.kl))
        .filter(d => methods.includes(d.method))
        .filter(d => d.age >= ages[0] && d.age <= ages[1])
        .filter(d => d.hc)
hc_found = hcf.length > 0
```

```{ojs}
{
  const btn = html`<button type="button" class="export-btn" ${hc_found ? "" : "disabled"}>Export this view</button>`;
  btn.addEventListener("click", () => exportView("highest_count", "kl_data", hcf, ["filter(!is.na(hc))"]));
  return html`<div class="export-row">${btn}<p class="export-note">Downloads a CSV of the ${hcf.length} rows shown below, plus an R script that reproduces this filtered selection.</p></div>`;
}
```

```{ojs}
)
```
